slides.title: Key-Value Store Overview
content: A key-value store is a distributed database that stores data as key and value pairs
Key acts as a unique identifier while value can be any data type
Optimized for fast access using direct key lookup
Designed for high scalability and low latency systems
Widely used in distributed applications and caching systems

slides.title: Why Key-Value Stores are Needed
content: Handles massive scale with millions of requests per second
Provides low latency for read and write operations
Simple data model reduces system complexity
Supports horizontal scaling across multiple nodes
Ideal for distributed environments and real-time systems

slides.title: Key Characteristics
content: Schema-less database design
Does not support joins or complex queries
Data is accessed only using keys
Designed for distributed storage systems
Focuses on performance and scalability

slides.title: CAP Theorem
content: A distributed system can guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance
Partition tolerance is mandatory in distributed systems
Systems must choose between consistency and availability
CP systems prioritize consistency over availability
AP systems prioritize availability over strict consistency

slides.title: Consistency Models
content: Strong consistency ensures reads always return latest data
Eventual consistency allows temporary stale data but converges over time
Weak consistency provides no strict guarantees but high performance
Choice depends on system requirements
Higher consistency often increases latency

slides.title: Data Partitioning
content: Partitioning divides data across multiple nodes
Improves scalability and performance
Reduces load on a single machine
Hash-based partitioning distributes data using key hashing
Naive hashing causes large data reshuffling when nodes change

slides.title: Consistent Hashing
content: Consistent hashing distributes keys across a circular hash ring
Keys are assigned to the nearest server in clockwise direction
Minimizes data movement when nodes are added or removed
Uses virtual nodes to improve load balancing
Essential for scalable distributed systems

slides.title: Replication
content: Replication stores multiple copies of data across nodes
Improves fault tolerance and availability
Replication factor defines number of copies
Leader-follower model uses a primary node for writes
Leaderless model allows any node to accept writes

slides.title: Quorum Mechanism
content: Quorum uses parameters N, R, and W for consistency control
N is total replicas, R is read acknowledgments, W is write acknowledgments
Strong consistency achieved when R plus W is greater than N
Ensures overlap between read and write operations
Trade-off exists between latency and consistency

slides.title: Versioning
content: Versioning tracks updates to detect conflicts
Helps maintain causality between operations
Timestamp method is simple but may have clock issues
Vector clocks track multiple versions accurately
Essential in distributed systems with concurrent updates

slides.title: Conflict Resolution
content: Conflicts occur during concurrent writes or network partitions
Last write wins uses latest timestamp but risks data loss
Vector clocks detect multiple versions of data
Application-level merge resolves conflicts using business logic
Proper conflict handling ensures data consistency

slides.title: Write Path
content: Client sends write request to coordinator node
Data is written to commit log for durability
Stored in in-memory structure called memtable
Replicated to multiple nodes
System waits for required acknowledgments before success

slides.title: Read Path
content: Client sends read request to coordinator node
Coordinator queries multiple replicas
Latest version of data is selected
Read repair updates stale replicas if needed
Final value is returned to client

slides.title: Failure Handling
content: Hinted handoff stores writes temporarily when node is down
Data is delivered later when node recovers
Permanent failures handled by rebuilding data from replicas
Gossip protocol helps nodes detect failures
Ensures system reliability and availability

slides.title: Storage Engine
content: Uses log structured merge tree for efficient storage
Writes are first stored in commit log
Memtable holds data in memory temporarily
Data is flushed to disk as SSTables
Compaction merges files to optimize storage

slides.title: Key Components
content: Memtable is an in-memory sorted data structure
SSTable is an immutable file stored on disk
Compaction merges multiple SSTables
Bloom filter helps check key existence quickly
Reduces unnecessary disk reads

slides.title: Important Concepts
content: Durability ensures data is not lost after write
Latency is the time taken to respond
Throughput is number of requests per second
Hotspot occurs when one node gets uneven load
Anti-entropy ensures replica synchronization

slides.title: Final Summary
content: Key-value stores provide scalable and high-performance data access
Use partitioning and consistent hashing for distribution
Replication and quorum ensure fault tolerance and consistency
Versioning and conflict resolution handle concurrent updates
LSM-tree storage enables efficient read and write operations
